heading: ## Repeated controls and gate registry — round 12
sectionize: frozen .ufo/evidence/round-18/measure.py (blob sha256 7ca87a7c98196d87a86627cf96e2e9bc7b3a8769496a75ce8caca1955b26dd37 at C0), loaded via importlib; sha256 independently reproduced by hashing lines 1521-1540 of the C0 blob with trailing blank lines stripped (1436 bytes, 19 lines)

findings.why: The parenthetical cites corpus/SOURCES.md:503 as the place the S026-to-S265 supersession is recorded, and that line does not record it at C0. Line 503 of corpus/SOURCES.md at C0 reads "- Next unused id: S265 (S261–S264 are map-only reserved; staged ids S161–S255 stay reserved by document for the package)." — a reserved-id bullet with no mention of S026. The supersession sentence is at corpus/SOURCES.md:506 at C0: "- Round 48: four rows added, S265-S268 (superseding held S026, S048, S093, S108; …). The two \"Next unused id: S265\" lines above were not updated in round 48; this line corrects them without rewriting." So the line the pointer lands on is one of the two stale bullets that the supersession record itself disclaims. The anchor was correct when written (99c3bc8, round-54 fix pass, changed 500→503) and then drifted: round-55's C0 (9cf0146) inserted one line above it (@@ -154,0 +155 @@) and round-56's C0 (c013745) inserted two more (@@ -155,0 +156,2 @@), moving the supersession sentence 503 → 504 → 506. It was already stale at the round-56 base 981c5e8b (503 = a 'Next unused id: S265' bullet, 504 = the supersession sentence). The substantive claim is true of the tree at C0 (SOURCES.md:140 carries the S265 row 'supersedes S026's anchor and quote only', and :506 records the round-48 supersession), and corpus/knowledge/repeated-control-precondition.md names 'S265 (supersedes S026)'; only the cited locator is wrong. Same defect class as the round-54 wave-1 finding T54W1Read11 on this same section, which the round-54 fix pass repaired by moving 500→503.

notes: Runner legs: the section's 'not a change to the six-leg runner of round 12' is true as a round-12 statement, but the tree's runner at C0 has ten legs (tools/mutate-and-run.sh:84 comment 'r4-2; r7-1 leg ledger; r10-2 six legs; r16 seven; r18 eight; r26 nine; r51 ten') and sha256 977de47034cbe52b87c3b4ba4a82ca334a6b88f1ef26d07dd59fd705649e0bda, not the round-12 pin 75ed934d…. The adjacent '### Gate/probe registry' section (a different heading, another seat's item) carries the correction ('The declaration's runner pin 75ed934d… is stale at round 27'), so this section is not self-contained on this point but is not false.

HYAKU_SCRATCH unset: the recipe's `$HYAKU_SCRATCH/tameshi-r12-controls-UNIQUE` expands to `/tameshi-r12-controls-UNIQUE` when the variable is absent, and the gate then refuses with `repeat-control: setup: cannot create --out /tameshi-r12-controls-T56W2Read06-unset: [Errno 13] Permission denied` and exit 2 (setup_error). The lane standing rules give the scratch root a default (/fast/scratch/hyaku, SKILL.md:28 and :164) but the recipe writes the bare variable; `${HYAKU_SCRATCH:-/fast/scratch/hyaku}` would make the recipe self-contained. Measured, not asserted by the section.

Scratch-path shape: the recipe's output directory `tameshi-r12-controls-UNIQUE` is a dash-form flat directory directly under the scratch root, while SKILL.md:28/164 prescribe `$HYAKU_SCRATCH/<lane>-r<round>/<sub>/` and state that the dash form 'survives only in run artifacts and quoted text of rounds 37-52, not as a live convention'. The command works either way; naming the standing shape would remove the tension.

Out-directory refusal code: the section states 'The output directory must not exist' but not the refusal's exit code. Measured at C0: a second run on an existing --out exits 64 with `repeat-control: --out already exists (refused, never overwritten)` and `REPEAT_CONTROL: invalid_usage`; the tool's selftest case `invalid-existing-out` asserts exactly that (expected=invalid_usage/64). Likewise `--runs 2` is refused with exit 64 ('--runs must be >= 3'), so the section's 'three or more' floor is enforced.

Cited knowledge note is stale about the very tool the section tells the reader to run: corpus/knowledge/repeated-control-precondition.md §3.1 states 'tools/repeat-control.py exists: 30,557 B, sha256 29d8025490f349c106bc8132da7bfecc2ae4f8fb00720b43636e52335d27467a' and locates 'the finding map :115-123, the precedence :191-205, the snapshot validator :337-435, the selftest :545'. At C0 the tool is 36,950 B, sha256 a8fad68fcbb87d03fb7e5e22fb1f70bd94d36c857a1c4b58171d91b042df80fd; EXIT_BY_ID is at :122-130, classify() at :238, snapshot_mode() at :481, selftest() at :624. The note carries a '## Round 16 note (append-only)' erratum for the runner pin but none for the round-53/round-55 tool edits, so a reader who follows the section's source pointer to the note gets the wrong tool revision and the wrong line map. The note's own finding→exit→class table is still correct — every row was re-measured at C0 (see findings/commands).

Round-12 receipt records an older tool revision: the section cites '.ufo/evidence/round-12/verification-final.json' as runtime evidence; that file's tool_sha256 is 296fe566dc59380b6baa518b61cef92fe3c7af09d538b2dde9e7f4af1b8cbc25 and its check list includes repeat-control-selftest (SELFTEST: PASS), frozen-match (controls_match/0), frozen-mismatch (controls_mismatch/1), real-pristine-three-controls (controls_match/0) and runner-six-leg-regression (REGRESSION: PASS); passed=true. Its recorded tool_sha256 is not the C0 tool's sha256, which is expected for a historical receipt and is not asserted as current by the section.

Verified true and unchanged: the section's three table rows match the tool at C0 exactly — three-or-more zero-exit identical controls → controls_match exit 0 (measured at 3 runs and 5 runs); any difference in exit or either stream → controls_mismatch exit 1; equal nonzero controls → baseline_nonzero exit 2; unavailable command → command_unavailable exit 2. The recipe's rules also hold at C0: the gate retries nothing, compares unnormalized bytes (the selftest case mismatch-newline-only passes, so a trailing-newline difference is a mismatch), and its own docstring states a clean match 'is not a determinism proof', matching the table's Bound column.

Verified true and unchanged: the recipe's caller-owns-timeout rule holds — with the caller wrapping the command in `timeout 10`, the gate produced no verdict (no finding.txt in the evidence dir) and the caller saw exit 124; the tool itself declares 'there is no timeout and no process supervisor' (tools/repeat-control.py:84-87) and has no signal/alarm/kill code.

Verified true and unchanged: SOURCES.md:15 carries the S004 row and :140 the S265 row, both listing corpus/knowledge/repeated-control-precondition.md as used-by; corpus/knowledge/repeated-control-precondition.md and .ufo/evidence/round-12/verification-final.json both exist at C0.
